messages:
michael-docs: quick note from triage: the README quickstart curl + python snippets disagree on the authentication header. curl uses Authorization: Bearer but python sample uses X-Api-Key. New users copy one and wonder auth fails.

michael-docs: curl snippet we ship:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hey"}'
```

kevin-support: saw two support tickets this morning complaining about 401s from the sample app. They copied the python sample into their Flask app and used X-Api-Key.

anya-devex: ugh. that's definitely a docs drift. Our server expects Authorization header for hosted, but Dedicated/private customers sometimes use X-API-Key via the load balancer. We should be explicit.

omar-sdk: proposed minimal change: standardize to Authorization: Bearer in all public quickstarts, but add a short note in Dedicated/Private section: "some enterprise load balancers accept X-API-Key; check your onboarding doc." Also patch the python sample to use requests with headers Authorization.

michael-docs: here's a suggested python snippet to replace the current one:
```py
import os
import requests

url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
headers = {'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
resp = requests.post(url, json={'model':'redwood-1','prompt':'hey'}, headers=headers)
print(resp.json()['output'])
```

kevin-support: also flagging that the python snippet doesn't show retry behavior. Some users hit a 503 during heavy load and assume the API is flaky. Can we add a one-line retry example or link to our retry policy?

anya-devex: yes. I'll add a 2-line retry note and link to the retry docs. We should avoid shipping a full retry loop in README, but a pointer and a 1s backoff suggestion is fine.

omar-sdk: while editing, please run the example snippets in examples/ci to catch header/name mismatches next time. I can add a mock server util that asserts the incoming header and returns a canned response.

ci-bot: created examples CI job: examples/snippet-smoke-tests (runs mock-server + snippet runners) — queued.

michael-docs: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/901 
Changes: canonicalize Authorization header, update python snippet, add short retry note, add Dedicated/Private note about X-API-Key.

kevin-support: thanks. also asked SRE to add a quick FAQ blurb for customers who copy snippets into Lambda environments where env var naming differs. We keep hitting variable naming noise (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY vs REDWOOD_TOKEN).

anya-devex: good catch. I'll standardize env var across repo and add a small line in CONTRIBUTING.md asking maintainers to prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY.

michael-docs: preview deploy: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/quickstart/901 — please sanity check.

ci-bot: examples CI passed for updated snippets (mock-server asserts Authorization header).

michael-docs: LGTM, merging after a small lint fix. Thanks team :rocket:

anya-devex: follow-up task: schedule a monthly docs snippet audit to run the smoke tests and catch regressions. Filing a ticket.

kevin-support: perfect. closing thread once PR is merged.
